 © 2026 Yahoo. All rights reserved. The game between the Jacksonville Jaguars and the Baltimore Ravens had all the hype sucked out of it after Lamar Jackson and Tyler Huntley both went down with injuries the previous week.
 As a result, what could have been a classic between two contenders turned into a one-sided rout. But near the end of the game, a comment from Al Michaels caught fans' attention. Seemingly referencing the bets made on the night, Michaels' remark drew mixed reactions from fans on social media.
 Advertisement Advertisement Advertisement Fans Aren't Sure What to Make of Al Michaels Referencing Betting Lines
 Gambling and sports betting have become an undeniable part of the NFL product these days. With a multitude of avenues for fans to invest more than just their time into the games, it remains a year-long conversation.
 However, this week, Michaels chose to have fun at the expense of the Jaguars and the Ravens late in the game. After they converted the extra point with less than 8 minutes remaining in the game, the scoreboard read 33-3.
 "There's some mini drama here now," Michaels jokingly remarked. "Does the number 39.5 mean anything to you?"
 It was a clear reference to the game's over/under total, which was listed at 39.5 at multiple sportsbooks before kickoff.
 Advertisement Advertisement Advertisement The drama didn't last long. Justice Hill immediately broke a 65-yard touchdown run, and Jake Moody's extra point made it 33-10, pushing the combined score to 43 and over the 39.5 total. But the comments still left a portion of the fans incensed.

 "Al needs to pack it in. Does he know that gambling is legal now in about 45 states? And
@KirkHerbstreit with that [expletive] laugh makes it cringier, plus the number doesn't even reach 39," one fan argued .
 Another fan believed it was a recurring theme for the veteran of the broadcasting booth, claiming, "I can't stand when he makes that stupid joke every game in primetime."
 For one fan, the problem with the comments was how prevalent gambling had become across the NFL. Rather than a novelty for a select few, it was an undeniable part of the experience, leaving them exhausted by the coverage.
 Advertisement Advertisement Advertisement "This felt fun when gambling was only in Vegas," the fan argued . "Now…It just feels like another gambling ad mixed in 2 hours of gambling ads with 20 min of football."
 Brandon McDermott seconded that opinion, adding, "Al still talks about the total like it's our little secret and we haven't spent three hours being told to download a sportsbook."
 However, even as some turned against him, there was a portion of the fan base that was unapologetically ecstatic about Michaels still calling games and the way he did it.
 While it rubbed some people the wrong way, Matt Warren confessed , "I do love it when he does this."
 "Al Michaels is still top dog imo, grew up listening to him on MNF," one fan claimed . "Classic voice."
 Advertisement Advertisement Advertisement SET YOUR LINEUPS: PFN's Free Fantasy Start/Sit Optimizer 
 He was far from the only one, as another fan added , "He's the OG bringing up gambling lines forever."
 It seems unlikely that Michaels is changing his broadcasting style this deep into his career. While he might rub some people the wrong way, there is clearly a section of fans that love the way he announces games.
